transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Well, I'm here because... I've been having this problem with eating. After I eat too much, I just go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I do it because I don't want to gain weight, but... it's gotten to the point where I'm doing it a lot, and I'm really scared I can't stop.
When you eat and then make yourself throw up, do you feel like you've lost control over how much you're eating during those times, or are you eating a normal amount on purpose?

It's definitely not a normal amount. I completely lose control. Once I start on those nights, it’s like... my hands just keep grabbing food. Even while I’m doing it, I’m in my head telling myself, 'Lucy, knock it off,' but I just can't stop. I don’t really feel like I'm back in charge of myself until it’s already done.

latest_inference.note: Patient describes loss of control during eating episodes followed by compensatory purging (self-induced vomiting). This is pathognomonic for Bulimia Nervosa, binge-eating/purging type (F50.02). F50.03 (binge-eating type without purging) is ruled out due to explicit purging behavior. F50.2 (Binge Eating Disorder) is ruled out as it lacks the compensatory purging mechanism.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with recurrent episodes of binge eating (loss of control, consumption of large quantities of food) followed by compensatory purging behavior (self-induced vomiting). The patient demonstrates clear loss of control during eating episodes, preoccupation with weight/shape, and regular purging behavior, meeting DSM-5/ICD-10 criteria for this diagnosis.
